headline: Digital Parking Permits and Maritime History Reservations
reservation: Tybee Island requires paid parking throughout the entire island, managed via physical kiosks or a mobile app. While general beach access is open, specific historical tours or lighthouse climbs may have capacity limits; check the official Tybee Island Light Station website for current entry protocols and potential closures.

days.title: Maritime Landmarks
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the North End

stops.name: Tybee Island Light Station
stops.detail: Climb the 178 steps of Georgia’s oldest and tallest lighthouse for panoramic views of the Savannah River.

stops.name: Tybee Museum at Battery Garland
stops.detail: Explore 400 years of history housed within a former coastal defense battery across from the lighthouse.

days.driving: Allow 10 minutes between sites; cycling is recommended to avoid parking transitions.
days.note: The lighthouse has strict weight and clothing rules for climbing; check official guidelines before arrival.

days.title: Estuary and Marsh Ecology

stops.name: Salt Marsh Kayaking
stops.detail: Paddle through tidal creeks to spot bottlenose dolphins and migratory shorebirds in the Spartina grass.

stops.name: Tybee Island Marine Science Center
stops.detail: Visit the interactive exhibits near the North Beach to learn about loggerhead sea turtle nesting habits.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes for travel; conditions vary with seasonal traffic on US-80.
days.note: Check local tide charts before kayaking, as low tides can expose impassable mudflats.

days.title: Atlantic Breezes and Piers

stops.name: Tybee Island Pier and Pavilion
stops.detail: Walk the iconic wooden pier for views of the Atlantic or watch local saltwater fishing.

stops.name: Back River Fishing Pier
stops.detail: Experience the quieter side of the island facing the marsh and Little Tybee Island.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes; parking is most competitive in the South Beach district.
days.note: Alcohol and glass are prohibited on all beaches; park rangers enforce local ordinances strictly.

intel.title: Island-Wide Paid Parking
intel.text: All public parking on Tybee is paid from 8 AM to 8 PM daily. Utilize the parking app to avoid citations, as enforcement is frequent near the North and South beach lots.

intel.title: Coastal Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service is generally robust across the island. Public Wi-Fi is available near the Pier, but speeds may vary during peak summer weekends.

intel.title: Mainland Transition
intel.text: Fuel stations are located along US-80 before crossing the bridge. It is advisable to refuel in Thunderbolt or Savannah where prices and availability are more consistent.

intel.title: Tidal Planning
intel.text: Beach width changes dramatically between high and low tide. Plan beach walks during receding tides to access more hard-packed sand and avoid being cut off by water.

intel.title: Fort Pulaski Gateway
intel.text: Access to the nearby Fort Pulaski National Monument is via the bridge to Cockspur Island. Check NPS hours as the gate closes promptly in the evening.

plan.arrival: Fly into SAV and pick up a rental for the 45-minute drive via the Islands Expressway. Stock up on supplies in Savannah before crossing the bridge onto Tybee.
plan.vehicle: Compact cars are ideal for navigating tight island streets and limited parking spots; check rental rules regarding beach driving, which is strictly prohibited.
plan.goldenHour: The Back River Pier is the premier spot for sunset views over the coastal marshes, varying seasonally.
